**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Transfer and Servicing Agreement imposes no non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction on the Issuer or Depositor, which satisfies the preferred position outright (rather than sitting at the fallback).

Key points:
- **No detection signals fired.** "compet" matched only "court of competent jurisdiction"; "shall not/will not engage", "solicit", and "territory" returned nothing; "exclusiv" matched only the Cap Collateral Account control mechanics and the non-exclusive jurisdiction clause.
- **Candidate homes are clean.** Article IX (Other Agreements) covers financing statements, expenses, no-petition, limited recourse, limitation of liability, tax treatment, risk retention and the Cap Collateral Account — no business-activity restriction. Article V (Depositor) is reps, liability and existence covenants.
- **Negative covenants on our side are structural, not vendor protections.** Section 9.2 (no transfer or lien on Transferred Property), Section 5.7 (no division) and Section 9.5 (no petition) are standard securitization bankruptcy-remoteness and collateral-integrity provisions. None restricts what businesses we operate or what products we buy or build, so they fall outside this rule.
- Per the planner note and rule scope, Permitted Activities limits on the Issuer arising under the Trust Agreement / structural covenants were not flagged.
